Sources from the talk

References and further reading

The source guide behind the action plan and prompt pack. Original references checked September 30, 2026; consult current documentation for settings and availability.

Download reference guide ↓

The prompts and fleet examples are proposed working aids. The four Explore, Build, Automate and Guide labels are the handout’s teaching framework.

[1] Four use patterns and workflows versus agents

  • Anthropic — Building effective agents — Explains predefined workflows versus agents that select steps. The four Explore/Build/Automate/Guide labels are this handout’s teaching framework, not an industry standard.

[2] Hosted service examples

  • OpenAI — ChatGPT Plus — Application features, limits and separate API billing.
  • Anthropic — Claude plans — Application capabilities, plans and feature availability.
  • Google — Gemini overview — Examples of Gemini assistant capabilities.
  • Microsoft — Copilot for business plans — Work-app integration and plan distinctions.
  • Grok — product overview — Examples of Grok capabilities.

[3] Tokens, subscriptions and API costs

  • OpenAI — Understanding and counting tokens — Input, output and reasoning-token concepts.
  • OpenAI — ChatGPT Plus — API usage is separately billed; subscriptions have limits.
  • LM Studio — Offline operation — Local model use is a separate deployment choice. The handout recommends starting with an approved hosted app, not buying hardware.

[4] Persistent instructions and better prompts

  • OpenAI — Custom instructions — Where user standing instructions are configured.
  • OpenAI — Projects in ChatGPT — Project instructions, files, sharing and project-scoped context.
  • OpenAI — Prompt engineering — Clear instructions, examples and relevant context; developer-oriented reference, not an API prerequisite.

[5] Session memory and safe retention

  • OpenAI — Memory in ChatGPT — Product memory controls and limitations.
  • Microsoft — Manage AI memory safety — Memory validation, access boundaries, freshness and poisoned-memory risks.
  • Anthropic — Effective context engineering — Curating relevant context and durable notes.

[6] Company knowledge and retrieval

  • Microsoft — Retrieval-augmented generation — Retrieval, grounding, document preparation and access control. Data-guide templates here are proposed working aids, not automatic data validation.

[7] Useful starting tools

  • OpenAI — Data analysis with ChatGPT — File analysis, calculation/code capabilities and supported workflows.
  • Anthropic — Writing tools for agents — Tool design and evaluation; tools expose specific operations.

[8] Tools versus skills

  • Anthropic — Agent Skills overview — Skills package reusable instructions and resources.
  • Anthropic — Equipping agents with skills — Skills can contain instructions, scripts and supporting materials; review their contents before enabling them.

[9] Verification and evaluation

  • OpenAI — Evaluation best practices — Representative tests, objectives, evaluation criteria and iteration.

[10] Security and unreliable output

  • OWASP — Prompt injection — Untrusted content can redirect model behavior; retrieval does not remove the risk.
  • OWASP — Excessive agency — Limit permissions and capabilities; retain approval for consequential actions.
  • OWASP — Misinformation — Incorrect output and overreliance risks.

For fleet planning and operating products, see the fleet-tool directory.
